title: Control-plane reconciliation delay causes tenant hostname misbind
creator: Amina Patel
description: Summary: Production customer (StrataWorks) reported intermittent cross-tenant hostname resolution where requests for tenant A occasionally resolved to tenant B's private hostnames for ~2-5 minutes after a rapid peering swap. Impact: user-facing API traffic for a subset of dedicated tenants returned 5xx or connected to wrong backend, causing data-plane misrouting and elevated error rates. Root cause: race between the peering control-plane reconciliation and our edge routing layer's cached tenant bindings. When a peering session was swapped (ordered shutdown + bringup across two peering endpoints), the control-plane published a new peering epoch but a subset of edge agents continued serving an older epoch long enough for their local DNS/route caches to respond to in-flight queries. The caches included per-tenant DNS reply mappings and ephemeral route bindings. The combination of a) fast peering swap, b) no strong fencing by epoch on the edge routing layer, and c) DNS replies cached with long TTLs led to brief cross-tenant hostname shadowing.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create two dedicated tenants (tenant-A, tenant-B) with VPC peering group configured.
2) Trigger peering swap: gracefully shutdown peering on node set 1 and bring up a new peering session on node set 2 within 30s.
3) Run high concurrency DNS resolution + short-lived connections from tenant-A while swap happens.
4) Observe occasional DNS replies that match tenant-B private hostnames on tenant-A flows for ~2-5 minutes on affected edge agents.
root_cause_analysis: Control-plane published peering epoch increment but edge agents apply peering change asynchronously.
Edge routing layer does not validate peering epoch when serving cached DNS/route entries; stale cached entries can be used for in-flight requests.
DNS replies were cached with TTLs inherited from internal resolvers; TTLs were not aggressively invalidated on peering swaps.
No metric or alert existed for 'peering epoch drift' between control-plane and edge observed state.
Race window widened by fast peering rotates from infra automation and peering heal attempts during customer failover tests.
fix_implemented: Added peering-epoch fenced apply in edge agents: cache entries now include a peering_epoch tag and are rejected if epoch != current active epoch.
On any peering state change we now emit a per-tenant DNS cache invalidation hook; edge agents perform targeted invalidation before marking peering active.
Reduced default internal DNS cache TTL for inter-tenant private hostnames from 60s to 5s during peering transitions; added exponential backoff to avoid thundering herd.
Backported fencing and invalidation to runtime-2.4.x branch; hotfix PR created and deployed to canary pool.
Added end-to-end integration test that simulates peering swap with concurrent DNS queries and asserts no cross-tenant answers.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (Canary, 10% edge pools) — 2026-02-28: hotfix runtime-2.4.1 deployed to canary; monitor for 24h.
Stage 2 (Gradual rollout, 50%) — 2026-03-02: expand to 50% with automated health gates on peering_epoch_drift and dns_misbind_rate.
Stage 3 (Global, 100%) — 2026-03-05: full rollout after gates pass for 72h.
Rollback plan: revert to pre-fix runtime build and re-enable TTLs; mitigation script to flush caches and force re-resolve if regression seen.
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: peering_epoch_drift > 1 for any tenant for more than 2m => P0 pager
SLO check: latency spike and 5xx increase guarded by synthetic probes per-tenant
customer_communication: 2026-02-12: On-call triaged and provided immediate mitigation steps to StrataWorks (temporary force-flush script and traffic routing to unaffected edge pool).
2026-02-27: After canary validation we sent post-fix summary and ETA for full rollout; invited StrataWorks to verification window.
2026-03-06: Final confirmation to customer that fix is fully deployed and monitoring shows no recurrence.
testing: Unit tests for peering_epoch fencing logic added (100% coverage for new module).
Integration test harness updated to simulate peering swaps and assert no cross-tenant DNS answers under high QPS.
Manual verification runbook: steps to simulate and validate per-tenant DNS isolation.
postmortem_actions: (1) Add peering epoch reconciliation audit: record last-applied epoch per-edge and surface drift in weekly report.
(2) Update peering automation to stagger swaps with a minimum guard window to allow caches to expire.
(3) Ship integration tests into CI that run a peering-swap test matrix on every release candidate.
(4) Reduce DNS cache TTLs for inter-tenant records in controlled release windows and make TTLs configurable per-tenant.
notes: This ticket consolidated customer escalations (StrataWorks) and internal infra findings; related long-term work tracked in project 'dedicated-isolation-harden'.
We decided not to implement global TTL reduction outside peering transitions due to cost of increased resolver load.
The hotfix required a minor schema bump to cache metadata; runtime rollback is straightforward if needed.
